Why 1.80 ha is needed for 100 bays; design vehicles and standards
Re-planned: 101 bays on 1.80 ha; full set
CAPACITY TEST-FIT — SAME LAYOUT STANDARDS ON BOTH SITES 1:500
41 bays (40 revenue) — 250 m² of land per bay
101 bays (100 revenue) — 180 m² of land per bay
Meets brief; all bays independently accessible
Why 1.0 ha cannot hold 100 bays: an 18.5 m articulated truck needs a 4.0 × 19.0 m bay (76 m²) plus half of a 17.5 m reversing aisle (35 m²) ≈ 111 m²
before any gate, stacking, amenities, drainage or perimeter. 100 bays therefore need ≈ 1.1 ha of pure parking; with the frontage zone (gate, 21.5 m
stacking, building, services ≈ 3 000 m²) and cross roads the minimum practical site is ≈ 1.7–1.8 ha. Narrower aisles or bays fail the swept-path
13.6°S, 1 250 m a.s.l.; sun to the north most of the year; rain Nov–Apr (≈ 1 100 mm/yr)
Building long axis E–W; verandah faces south (shaded); PV + SWH on north slope at 15°
East / south-east (dry season); high-level vents on both long walls
Ng 8–12 flashes/km²/yr — LPS to masts, building and fence earthing
Laterite / residual soils on Irumide basement; presumed 150 kPa at 0.7 m (BS 8004 Tab. 1)
≈ 2 × 10⁶ E80 over 20 years; ICBP on cemented subbase
≥ 1 interlink clear of T2 carriageway (37.5 m to entry boom)
One-way clockwise loop; 10 km/h; no reversing on through routes
20 lx average yard, U0 0.25; 300 lx lounge / office
